reference: GNU coreutils expand, invoked through PATH in the reference run, provides independent byte-for-byte output and status comparisons. Invalid-option usage status and builtin metadata use the documented Bash-OS/Bash contract; help availability is checked with Bash's help builtin.
coverage: Default eight-column stops and newline resets
Initial-only conversion, explicit stops, and backspace behavior
Finite stops, /N extension, +N extension, and repeated -t options
Column state across multiple files and unterminated file boundaries
Stdin interleaved with files and repeated '-' operands
NUL and control-byte preservation with byte-column accounting
Long-option aliases, options after operands, and -- for a dash-leading filename
Missing-file failure while processing a valid file
Fresh options and column state on repeated calls in one shell
Bash type/help metadata and documented invalid-option usage status
exclusions: Terminal newline flush while input remains open is deferred because this runner has no PTY driver or synchronized producer/consumer fixture.
Very large records, output-device failures, signal behavior, and cross-libc behavior are outside this compact suite.

cases.purpose: Compare default eight-column expansion and verify that each newline resets the next tab's column.
Compare -i with an initial blank, a tab after the first nonblank, and backspace before a later tab; explicit stops are included.
Compare finite explicit stops, repeated -t stop accumulation, and the distinct GNU /N and +N extension rules.
cases.script:
printf '	X	Y	Z
' | expand -t 3,7
printf '	X	Y	Z
' | expand -t 3 -t 7
printf '	X	Y	Z
' | expand -t '3,7,/5'
printf '	X	Y	Z
' | expand -t '3,7,+5'

cases.purpose: Compare the documented single-stream behavior: column state carries across an unterminated file boundary and resets after a newline.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > first
printf '\tX\n' > second
printf 'q\tR\n' > third
expand first second third

cases.purpose: Compare stdin as part of the file stream, including column continuity from a file into stdin and onward to a later file; a second '-' sees the exhausted stream.
cases.script:
printf 'ab' > left
printf '\tR' > right
printf 'c\tS' | expand left - right -

cases.purpose: Compare preservation of NUL, backspace, carriage return, and other bytes while tab columns count bytes and handle backspace/newline specially.
Compare GNU long-option aliases after a file operand, then verify that -- permits reading a relative filename beginning with a dash.
cases.script:
printf ' \tA\tB\n' > input
expand input --initial --tabs=4
printf '\tD\n' > -draft
expand -- -draft

cases.purpose: Verify that a valid operand is still processed when another file cannot be opened, and that expand returns failure with a diagnostic.
cases.script:
printf 'a\tb\n' > good
if expand good absent; then exit 91; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]

cases.purpose: Run both commands directly in one persistent shell, with different options and the same reopened input, to check option and column reset.
cases.script:
printf 'a\tX' > input
expand -t 4 < input
expand < input

cases.purpose: Check the documented Bash loadable metadata contract without invoking an external command: type identifies expand as a builtin and help has an entry.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t expand) == builtin ]] || exit 90
help expand >metadata.txt
printf 'builtin\nhelp-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Reject descending tab stops with failure status 1 and a diagnostic.
cases.script:
if printf '\tX' | expand -t 3,2; then exit 91; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]

cases.purpose: Check terminal output delivery at newline while expand input remains open.
cases.reason: Requires a PTY and a synchronized producer/consumer that can write one line, observe output before EOF, then close the input. The declarative fixture runner captures stdout in a regular file and has no PTY driver; perform this in a future disposable VM with an isolated PTY harness.

cases.purpose: Compare GNU invalid-tablist status directly; retain any usage-status difference despite the separate documented Bash contract.
